title: Adaptive SLO-driven traffic throttle and stream safeguard for active-active gateways
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement an active-active edge/gateway failover mechanism that is SLO-aware and preserves streaming/session continuity while providing safe automatic load shedding via rate-aware circuit breakers. This ticket covers the protocol and implementation tasks for adaptive traffic shifting, session token grafting for long-lived streams, KV cache lease reconciliation, telemetry-driven cutover thresholds, and an SLO-first rollback policy.

Scope: hosted API edge (global gateway), not Dedicated or Private control plane. Includes: steering service changes, gateway proxy handshake updates, runtime token stitcher, telemetry and alerting updates, runbook and chaos tests. Excludes: model runtime internals and customer SDK changes (those will be handled in a follow-up integration ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Weighted traffic shift policy that can perform gradual shifts with per-connection stream handshake and token grafting
Circuit breaker tier that uses combined signals (region p99 latency, error rate, capacity headroom) to start progressive load shedding with target SLO preservation
KV cache lease reconciliation ensures prefix hits for streamed sessions are preserved for at least 30s during handoff
End-to-end tests that simulate region outage and validate zero-stream data loss for >95% of active streams (other than intentionally shed connections)
Runbook documented and tested with a chaos engineering run that exercises threshold crossings and automated rollback
design_notes: Primary design: SLO-driven controller evaluates regional telemetry every 250ms and computes per-route shift fraction using a PID-like controller capped by a configurable ramp-rate
Session continuity: introduce transient token grafting where outgoing edge provides a signed short-lived continuation token that incoming edge can validate and stitch into its local session table
Streaming handshake: extended 3-way handshake at the proxy layer for active stream handoff — REQUEST -> PREPARE -> ACK — allows upstream runtime to snapshot in-flight KV and reply buffer offsets
KV cache: implement lease metadata with monotonic 'lease_epoch' that can be reconciled; prefer last-writer-wins on short epochs to reduce split-brain state
Circuit breakers: multi-dimensional breaker combining latency, error-rate, queue depth; breakers operate with hysteresis and two-phase shedding (graceful throttles then connection eject)
decisions: Use steering-service centralized policy evaluation (instead of fully distributed per-gateway) to simplify global SLO reasoning and allow coordinated shifts
Adopt weighted gradual shift with session pinning window of 10s to reduce reconnect churn for short synchronous requests
Token grafting chosen over proxy-level stream proxying to avoid per-token proxying overhead and keep runtime statelessness guarantee
Expose tuning knobs via console (ramp_rate, max_shift_per_minute, shedding_thresholds) for SRE/enterprise customers

implementation_notes: We will first ship a non-streaming pilot that validates weighted shift logic using normal request paths before enabling handshake changes for streaming sessions
Fallback behavior: if token grafting verification fails on incoming edge, connection should fall back to normal reconnect path with telemetry tagging for analysis
To minimize customer impact, initial rollout gated behind feature flag and internal-only traffic for 2 weeks
Telemetry knobs: steering-service will emit proposed_shift, applied_shift, reason_codes (latency|errors|capacity) for each evaluation interval
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: token graft misuse could open replay window. Mitigation: short TTL (<=10s) and one-time-use nonce tied to session-id
Risk: reconciling KV epoch conflicts may cause transient cache misses that increase latency. Mitigation: prioritize correctness for streaming handoff and allow small grace TTL of cached prefixes
Risk: over-eager shedding could cause SLA violations for premium customers. Mitigation: implement customer tier-aware policies and never fully eject premium lanes without manual confirmation
